concept.name: Fama-French five-factor model
concept.definition: An extension of the Fama-French three-factor model (Fama and French 2015, 'A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model') that adds a profitability factor, RMW (robust minus weak operating profitability), and an investment factor, CMA (conservative minus aggressive asset growth), to the market, size, and value factors.
concept.intuition: Beyond market, size, and value, two more dials matter: profitable firms tend to beat unprofitable ones, and firms that invest conservatively tend to beat firms that expand aggressively.
concept.mechanics: R_i - R_f = alpha_i + b_i*(R_m - R_f) + s_i*SMB + h_i*HML + r_i*RMW + c_i*CMA + e_i. The factors are built from 2x3 value-weight sorts on size paired with book-to-market, operating profitability, and investment; SMB is averaged across the three pairings.
concept.formula: R_i - R_f = alpha_i + b_i*(R_m - R_f) + s_i*SMB + h_i*HML + r_i*RMW + c_i*CMA + e_i.
concept.failure_modes: Even five factors leave momentum and several anomalies unexplained, and Fama and French note the model's main problem is the low average returns of small stocks that invest a lot despite low profitability; HML becomes redundant for describing average returns once RMW and CMA are included.
concept.misconceptions: More factors do not mean a complete model of returns - the five-factor model is still an empirical approximation whose factor premia vary across periods and markets.
concept.example: A highly profitable, low-asset-growth fund shows positive RMW and CMA loadings in a five-factor regression, which can absorb what looked like alpha under the three-factor model.

citations.source: Kenneth R. French Data Library, Description of Fama/French 5 Factors (2x3)
citations.section: Construction; reference to Fama and French (2014/2015), A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model
